conflicts.fact: Kajiado panel/pump power data (morning vs afternoon)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: morning 18 °C partly cloudy 420 W vs afternoon 35 °C full sun 310 W (pump output). Lesson 3: morning 310 W vs afternoon 210 W (panel output). Same phenomenon, different datasets; Lesson 3 morning value equals Lesson 1 afternoon value.

conflicts.fact: Physical mechanism explaining why heat reduces output
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3: higher mobility lowers/higher lattice scattering reduces mobility and open-circuit voltage. Lesson 5: thermal electron-hole pairs reduce built-in voltage and open-circuit voltage (not mobility). Lesson 6: lattice vibrations reduce mobility and current. Lesson 7: lattice vibrations increase electron-hole recombination, reducing current. Incompatible mechanisms presented as the explanation.

conflicts.fact: Silicon conduction band occupancy at room temperature
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2: conduction band mostly empty with only a few electrons jumping. Lesson 3: teacher checks that the silicon column shows a partially filled conduction band, not empty; conduction band cards include 'partially filled' for silicon.

conflicts.fact: Role of band gap and energy source in explanation; darkness conduction
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2: band gap ~1.1 eV matched to visible light so sunlight (light) pushes electrons across; heat/temperature explanation postponed. Lesson 3: thermal promotion of electrons across gap at room temperature. Lesson 7: gap large enough to block flow in darkness. Lesson 1/2 circuit test showed silicon conducting dimly with a 1.5 V battery without light.
Lesson 1: silicon glows dimly. Lesson 2: silicon gave only a faint flicker, and only in bright light.

conflicts.fact: Silicon band gap value and insulator gap; lesson numbering of energy band introduction
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2: ~1.1 eV and introduces energy bands in Lesson 2; Lesson 3 gives 1.12 eV and presents the energy band model as newly introduced, and Lesson 2 says electron-hole pairs come in Lesson 3 while Lesson 4 says band-gap model was built in Lesson 3 (and 'last lesson').

conflicts.fact: Location of the solar panel case study and temperature range
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 uses Turkana/Lodwar panels at 15–45 °C while the anchoring phenomenon is Kajiado at 18–35 °C; Lesson 6 also adds superconductors/MRI as 'same family of semiconductor properties', contradicting semiconductor definition elsewhere.

conflicts.fact: Lesson where p-n junction explains temperature effect
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says Lesson 5 will explain why high temperatures reduce power via junction; Lesson 3 already claims a full mechanism; Lesson 3 also says doping is for later while Lesson 4 says the junction, not temperature, controls direction.
